thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: multi-region failover initiated for eu-central1 -> eu-west1. Traffic-shift stuck at ~95% to eu-west1; cloud DNS shows mixed records. Multiple customer 5xx reports. Pager triggered.

sam (oncall): acked — I'm on it. grabbing the runbook now. first pass: validate healthchecks and active weights.

liz (sre): seeing elevated 503s in frontend metrics for eu-central1 origin group. Backend healthchecks for eu-central1 are green in our control plane but external probes show failures.

raj (netops): I can confirm BGP announcements from eu-central1 look fine. However, authoritative DNS (cloud-dns) seems to be serving a mix of old and new endpoints. TTLs are 60s but some caches still return old values.

sofia (on-call): customer impact: partial — ~20% of EU requests hitting eu-central1 are erroring out; overall EU errors up ~8% in last 5m. Not a full outage but large degradation.

sam (oncall): trying a manual rollback of the traffic-shift to 50/50. applying weight change now.

eli (eng): wait — rollback might route traffic back to unhealthy instances in eu-central1. can we put eu-central1 in draining mode first?

sam (oncall): good point. putting eu-central1 pools to draining. command: ```redwoodctl pool set-status eu-central1 frontend draining --reason "traffic-shift rollback"```

liz (sre): copy that — setting LB weights to 50/50 now. ```aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:... --default-actions "Forward to targetGroupA weight=50,targetGroupB weight=50"``` (pseudo)

raj (netops): running dig against the authoritative names: ```;; ANSWER SECTION:\nservice.redwood.example.com. 60 IN A 35.203.12.5\nservice.redwood.example.com. 60 IN A 34.102.98.7``` looks mixed between regions. Some edge caches still have the previous A set.

mike (prodops): Are we using Cloud CDN/edge caches that need purging? If caches hold the old IPs, clients will continue to hit eu-central.

sofia (on-call): purge in progress for edge-cache region eu. ticket #EDGE-3921.

sam (oncall): adding temporary DNS emergency TTL override to 10s on authoritative records to speed convergence. ```gcloud dns record-sets transaction start --zone=redwood-eu && gcloud dns record-sets transaction add ... --ttl=10``` (placeholder)

raj (netops): FYI that TTL override may take one TTL cycle to propagate to some resolvers, but it should speed things. also verifying Cloud DNS global sync — there was a delayed change propagation in one diffusion partition. submitting support ticket to cloud provider.

liz (sre): metrics: 503s in eu drop from 8% -> 3% after LB weight change and draining. latency for eu-west slightly increased but within SLO. still seeing intermittent failures for particular ASNs.

eli (eng): logs show connection resets from a subset of upstream proxies in eu-central. Could be NAT exhaustion during the shift. I'm increasing ephemeral port pool on the NATs and rolling a tiny config change.

sam (oncall): great. apply and confirm.

eli (eng): applied NAT tweak on eu-central NAT gateway group. No config restart required. monitoring.

mike (prodops): customer comms drafted: "We're seeing partial traffic routing issues in EU, engineering is engaged and we are mitigating. We'll update in 30 minutes or on resolution." Want me to send?

sofia (on-call): send now. include affected endpoints list and temporary mitigation (50/50 rollback + draining).

raj (netops): cloud provider responded: there was an internal DNS partition re-sync delay in eu-central; their engineering team forced re-sync and confirmed all authoritative nodes now serve the same records.

sam (oncall): edge purge completed across eu. DNS TTL lowered. LB weights at 70% eu-west / 30% eu-central while we validate.

liz (sre): error rate trending down to baseline. I'll keep 24/7 alerting escalated for next 2 hours.

sofia (on-call): handing over to night oncall @raj in 20m. I'm staying reachable for questions.

raj (netops): taking over oncall. notes: watch for cache re-population, NAT port usage, and provider DNS stability. escalation plan: promote eu-central back to full only after 30m of stable healthchecks and <1% error.

sam (oncall): incident status: mitigated -> partial impact reduced. initiating post-incident ticket with timeline and RCA starters.

incident-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-3034. Postmortem assigned to liz, due in 72h.

mike (prodops): thumbs up on quick mitigation. action items: 1) add provider DNS sync check to our pre-shift gating, 2) automate emergency TTL override in runbook, 3) NAT ephemeral pool alerting. I'll triage and add to backlog. :thumbsup:

sofia (on-call): leaving thread for handoff. thanks team. :pray:

raj (netops): final note before close: no customer data exposure. primary root cause appears to be provider-side DNS partition delay + edge cache lag during aggressive traffic-shift.

sam (oncall): closing thread; follow-ups in INC-2026-3034 and postmortem. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
